title: Wracklebeak's Regrowing Quills
story: Wracklebeak guards the seabird nests on the Ternstone Cliffs, firing quills at anyone who climbs near. Mr 6 discovers that each quill he plucks free causes 2 new quills to sprout — a bad trade, unless you plan ahead. The rescue party needs the quill count down to zero to reach the trapped chicks.
question: Wracklebeak starts with 9 quills. Each time Mr 6 plucks 3 quills at once, only 1 new quill sprouts back. How many pluck-of-three actions does it take to bring him to exactly 1 quill?
hint: Each pluck-of-three changes the total by minus 3 plus 1. Track it: 9, then 7, then...
victory: After the fourth pluck, Wracklebeak was down to one lonely quill and used it as a toothpick. He handed over the nests, admitted defeat, and asked Mr 6 to teach him subtraction.
imagePrompt: A bristling seabird-porcupine perched on a windy cliff ledge above crashing waves, quills shrinking as a tiny caped numeral 6 counts on his fingers.
